items.note: Survey of 1,443 Egyptian tourism students (PLS-SEM) linking perceived ChatGPT risks to creative thinking, plus an SPSS quasi-experiment comparing ChatGPT users; creative thinking is likely a self-reported scale, so it may be out as self_report_only after full text.

Children trained with the Co-Art voice-to-image co-creation system drew pictures rated higher in aesthetics, richness, imagination, and creativity than a non-trained group; sample size and assignment not stated.

Online network experiments in which humans and AI agents in human-only, AI-only, and hybrid 5x5 networks iteratively modify stories, with rated creativity and collective diversity; abstract gives no N (search notes cite 1,363 to 1,473 humans); PsyArXiv version of arXiv 2502.17962 (CogSci 2025).

43 NLP researchers randomly assigned to execute an LLM-generated or expert-written research idea, with executed papers blind-reviewed for novelty and other metrics; the AI varies the input idea rather than assisting the work, and N is below 50.

Single-group pretest-posttest study of Chilean 12-13-year-olds who wrote songs with ChatGPT, with TTCT fluency, flexibility, and originality measured before and after (after_ai); no control group and N not stated in the abstract.

120 undergraduates in a character design course assigned to GAI with structured design thinking, GAI without strategy, or traditional learning; design achievement likely scored on produced designs, plus self-efficacy and problem-solving.

46 participants completed creative design tasks in a serious game with or without generative AI; creative outputs were scored for quantity, quality, and elaboration, alongside physiological stress; N below 50.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC); search notes say 128 participants in generative-AI versus traditional groups did brainstorming and TRIZ design tasks, with creativity output scores plus fNIRS and facial-expression measures.

132 nursing undergraduates randomly divided into a GenAI-based interactive teaching group and a control group; outcomes are higher-order thinking skills and AI literacy scores, not creativity scored on a creative output (HOTS scale may include a creativity subscale; check if needed).

Controlled experiment (N = 398) with Human-Only, Standard Chatbot, Engage-to-Unlock, and Time-Matched Unlock conditions on a writing task; reported outcomes are effort allocation, prompting, and evaluation accuracy, so it is unclear whether writing quality or creativity is scored.
